channel.title: Government Contracting Information
channel.description: Practical guides, market intelligence and industry news for small businesses competing in federal government contracting — SAM.gov, SBA certifications, GSA Schedules, proposals and capture management.

item.title: SAM.gov Registration in 2026: The Complete Small Business Guide
item.description: Entity validation, UEI numbers, CAGE codes and annual renewals — everything a small business needs to register on SAM.gov the right way the first time.

item.title: 8(a) vs HUBZone vs SDVOSB vs WOSB: Which Certification Should Your Small Business Pursue?
item.description: Each SBA certification unlocks a different slice of set-aside spending. Here is how to match your ownership profile and location to the highest-value certification.

item.title: Is a GSA Schedule Worth It for a Small Business? An Honest Analysis
item.description: A GSA Schedule is a $50B+ buying channel — but it is also a multi-month commitment with real costs. Here's the math on when it pays off and when it doesn't.

item.title: Sources Sought Responses: How to Shape a Contract Before It Exists
item.description: The Sources Sought notice is your earliest — and cheapest — chance to influence a solicitation. Most small businesses ignore it. Here's how to write a response that moves the needle.

item.title: The Proposal Compliance Matrix: The Document That Prevents Auto-Elimination
item.description: Before you write a word of your proposal, build a compliance matrix. This one document is the difference between a scored proposal and a rejected one.

item.title: NAICS Code Selection: The Quiet Decision That Determines Your Entire Federal Market
item.description: Your NAICS codes decide which size standard applies to you, which set-asides you qualify for, and which opportunities you ever see. Here's how to choose well.

item.title: The Capability Statement That Actually Gets Responses
item.description: Most capability statements are brochures. Contracting officers need a one-page decision document. Here is the structure that gets you on their vendor lists.

item.title: Teaming Agreements for Small Businesses: How to Bid on Contracts You Can't Win Alone
item.description: Teaming lets a small business combine capabilities with a larger partner to bid work neither could win alone. Here's how the structures work and what to watch for.

item.title: The Federal Budget Cycle: When Contracts Actually Get Awarded
item.description: Federal buying has a rhythm driven by the fiscal year. Knowing when money gets appropriated, obligated and expires tells you when to be ready.

item.title: Set-Asides, Simplified: How Small Businesses Get a Head Start on Federal Contracts
item.description: Total small business set-asides, partial set-asides, 8(a) sole-source, HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB — what each means and how to know which ones you qualify for.
